preRegisteredFalsifier.statedBeforeCounting: Mechanism A (ours) is what I expect to find if the 2026-vintage record-1 Property file, counted directly and independently of our own ingest, contains a distinct-PropertyID population MATERIALLY ABOVE 134,606 -- specifically approaching the 172,116 baseline (a result in, say, the 150,000-172,000 band would mean our ingest dropped a large fraction of a genuinely larger source and A is likely). Mechanism B (theirs) is what I expect if an independent recount of the source lands at or near 134,606 (within normal roll-to-roll churn, call it +/-1-2%) -- that means 134,606 is faithfully what Hays CAD's own 2026 export contains and re-acquiring the same source changes nothing. A result of exactly 134,606 on a re-count of the SAME file our ingest used would be a strong but not sufficient A-rule-out on its own (it would only prove our parser read that one file completely, not that the file itself is complete); the discriminating test is counting a DIFFERENT, independently-drawn 2026 vintage from the same county and checking whether it lands in the same place.
preRegisteredFalsifier.wouldNotBeAFalsifierIfTrue: If I had only re-read cad_property's own row count and called that 'the source count,' that would prove nothing (it's the same number by construction) and is explicitly the DEV_PROCESS 4.1 violation the dispatch warns against ('reading the store to guess at the ingest is reading a proxy for the authoritative record'). The falsifier requires fetching bytes Hays CAD serves today, outside our pipeline, and counting them with the same rule our parser uses.
preRegisteredFalsifier.fired: NO -- for mechanism A. Three independent source counts (below) cluster tightly around 134,600 across a 5-month span and two different export schemas; none approaches the 172,116 band. Mechanism A is ruled out by this falsifier. Mechanism B is what the data shows.

step1b_the172116BaselineIsNotACleanCadCo.whatIFound: P:/doc_repo/_inbox/2026-08-25_p78_announce_hays_48209.md, a filed and already-applied P-78 leftover fill, documents that on 2026-08-25 a StratMap parcel/land-use geometry fallback (TxGIO StratMap 202503 zip, NOT a Hays CAD export) was applied to tax_year 2025 ONLY for county 48209, explicitly stated 'Declared 2026 rows unchanged.' Before-measure was 131246 rows at tax_year 2025; after, 172116 (116421 rows upserted, of which 40870 were net-new keys, the remainder in-place updates to already-existing 2025 PKs whose source_file attribution the upsert overwrote). This fallback exists BECAUSE the original 2025 CAD-only population was already known to be incomplete (131246, itself short of 172116) -- it is a documented patch for exactly the kind of gap this dispatch is investigating, applied one tax year earlier and to a different, non-CAD source.
step1b_the172116BaselineIsNotACleanCadCo.consequence: 172116 was never a single-source, single-vintage CAD roll count. It is a genuine Hays CAD 2025 export layered with a StratMap parcel-geometry supplement applied for coverage, not appraisal completeness. Comparing 134606 (2026, one CAD-only source, one ingest, one 33-second window) against 172116 (2025, two source lineages of different classes, applied five weeks apart) compares two different classes of number -- DEV_PROCESS 1.3/1.4. This does not change the A-vs-B verdict below, which rests on the independent source recount, not on this comparison; it explains why the shrinkage looked as large as it did, and means the dispatch's own fallback instruction under mechanism A ('target: a roll not smaller than 2025 without a named reason') would itself need re-scoping if this were A, since 2025's own number already isn't a clean bar. It is not A, so this does not need to be resolved now, but it is filed here as a finding in its own right.

step2_sourceCount.verdict: Three independent Hays-sourced counts, spanning 2026-03 through 2026-08-27 and two different export schemas, converge on 134591-134606-134600 (a spread of 15 rows, 0.01%). None approaches 172116 or even a meaningfully-larger neighborhood. MECHANISM B (theirs): Hays CAD's own 2026 roll genuinely contains ~134,600 accounts. This is not an artifact of our acquisition.
